device: The deck's sage tile, grown into the photograph
lede: (the bench photograph above; below it the brand deck's sage tile. the deck's tulips rise out of the panel as sage paper silhouettes across the seam and become watercolour inside it; the white wordmark sits over them exactly as on the box; the tool is the headline.)
idea: The first pass put a painted dahlia, an embroidery band and loose petals on the bench, and it looked stuck on. The deck's system is simpler and stronger: a flat sage ground, soft watercolour tulips, the wordmark in white over them. So the lower half of each card is now that tile, built from the deck's own tulip cluster keyed out of the brand-look page, and the integration is a single move: the tulip cluster is drawn twice at the same spot, once as a sage silhouette that rises above the seam into the photograph like cut paper, once as watercolour clipped to the panel. Nothing sits on the photograph but the brand's own colour. The tool's name is the headline; the figures are the listing's.
type: White Velista at up to 132px on sage; a Cormorant italic aside; three figures in Jost 600 under mono keys, all in white. The white wordmark from the deck's dark logo page at 280px, right of the copy column, over the tulips. The silhouette is a CSS mask of the tulip cut-out filled with the sage; the watercolour beneath it is clipped by the panel's top edge. Foot in white; CTA white with sage type.
review: Editor's pass on the redo: the deck's caption text had come through the keying and showed at the seam; the white wordmark collided with the price. Fixed: the caption rectangle cleared from the cut-out, the wordmark raised clear of the foot. Dahlia, embroidery band, petals and watermark all removed. Plates as verified before; the one-unit stud is still cropped out of the loupe frame in both formats.
verdict: THE CALLIPER. leads and is the only hero-stock card; the rest are brand pieces until the ring and the set restock.

B1.title: THE CALLIPER.
B1.why: The braided hoop in the calliper's jaws; sage tulips rising across the seam; twenty-five across.

B2.title: THE MANDREL.
B2.why: The chevron on the brass mandrel. A fixed size is a single number, and the card prints it.
B2.check: US 7, 17.3mm inside, 9.5mm at the chevron on JDR0303312-7; 5 units, non-hero card.

B3.title: THE LOUPE.
B3.why: The halo band under the loupe, the neighbouring stud cropped out because it has one unit.
B3.source: Bench frame B02, cropped in both formats.
B3.check: 8mm stone, 12mm halo, US 7 on WR10170K7; 3 units, non-hero card.

B4.title: THE EAR.
B4.why: The fluted-disc hoop on the ear. The only bench tool with a pulse.
B4.check: 22mm across, 6mm discs on FE03586B; 4 units, non-hero card.

B5.title: THE GRID.
B5.why: The clover huggie on engineering paper. Engineering paper does not round up.
B5.check: 8.5mm drop, 10.2mm huggie on JDE0201327; 3 units, non-hero card.
